newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, rebound seen next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, rebound seen next week.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the fourth consecutive session on Friday but analysts expected them to rebound sometime early next week on the back of the session's strong buying after price-fixing.

The main market's WIG index fell 89.3 points, or 0.7 percent, to 13,568.1 and turnover rose 10 percent to 93.9 million zlotys ($33.1 million) on both markets as 32 issues fell, 21 rose and 24 were flat.

They also said that though slight falls could follow the rebound, this week's profit-taking correction after 11.6 percent growth since mid-August was likely to end above 13,000 points of the WIG index and the market could return to growth.
"The bourse should rebound on Monday or on Tuesday, and the correction should end above 13,000 or even above 13,500," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
Some analysts said, however, that the bourse could extend losses to 12,300 points of the WIG index before rebounding.

None of the stocks quoted in the continuous trade system saw action on Friday. Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.9 percent in a record 32.7-million-zloty turnover ($11.9 million) in the regular session and rose 3.4 percent in 2.1-million-zloty ($0.8 million) continuous trade.
